<thought>Based on the high‑resolution mass spectrum, the monoisotopic [M+H]⁺ peak is at m/z 183.0451. Subtracting the mass of a proton gives a neutral mass of ~182.037 Da. A plausible molecular formula that matches this mass and contains one chlorine atom is C₁₀H₁₁ClO (exact monoisotopic mass 182.0498 Da, within typical HR‑MS error). This formula yields an integer double‑bond equivalent and is consistent with the observed chlorine isotopic pattern (M+2 peak ≈ 33 % of the base peak). A common structure with this formula is **4‑chlorobenzyl acetone** (4‑chlorophenyl propan‑2‑one), whose SMILES representation is `CC(=O)CC1=CC=C(C=C1)Cl`. This SMILES is valid, matches the formula C₁₀H₁₁ClO, and is chemically reasonable for the observed data.** 

<final_answer>CC(=O)CC1=CC=C(C=C1)Cl</final_answer>
